Members cross and project beyond joints instead of resolving into a solid box. Visible wear and the photographed seat's darkness should not be converted into an invented universal palette measurement.

media.title: Zig-Zag Chair
media.creator: Gerrit Thomas Rietveld

observations.observation: Four broad pale planar boards form a continuous zig-zag chair with open sides and a diagonal structural support. Worn edges and visible joins demonstrate a physical object. This later Rietveld design broadens the furniture context; a rule forbidding all diagonals in all related three-dimensional work would be inaccurate. Kept outside qualifying corpus as a later related 1934 design rather than core 1917–31 evidence.

summary.scope: 20 Mondrian paintings/study, six Van Doesburg paintings/counter-compositions, one Rietveld chair, three journal cover designs. Still media only. Painting-heavy, scant architecture and other De Stijl members; later diagonal branch distinguished from Neo-Plasticism. Commons metadata traces diverse museums, catalogue/reprint and auction images; exact color and typography metrics unknown.
